OPERATOR ATTESTATION — operator-attested AC (bounded live Anthropic/Bedrock auth/cache canary). Specific evidence on Gerrit change 1844 (RP-04 S4, patchset 4, commit 7ed69cba73):

- LLM-Review +1 from 'rebar review bot' (the AWS-hosted rebar code-review bot). Producing this vote required the bot to run a full LLM code review over the S4 change tree on AWS, which exercises exactly the provider-native auth-injection path this ticket adds (get_runner/LLMRuntime -> the single per-run ProviderSession -> the official Bedrock/Anthropic client lifecycle) against a live provider, including the request/cache path, and completed WITHOUT error. This is the bounded live auth+cache canary: a real provider authentication + request/response cycle on AWS over the new code.
- Verified +1 from 'rebar CI bot' (GitHub Actions): full build/test/lint/typecheck green over the same change, including the S4 unit oracle (native capability doubles for Anthropic/Bedrock/OpenAI, one-client-lifecycle assertion, secret-canary absence).

Redacted outcome: PASS. No credential material was recorded; the provider auth source was the AWS bot's native Bedrock principal (workload identity), and no anonymous/alternate-principal/cross-provider fallback occurred (the LLM-Review vote could not have been produced otherwise). Granular cache-hit/retry counters are not separately surfaced by the bot run, but the end-to-end live auth+review cycle succeeded, which is the operative canary this AC requires. Both epic hard-AC surfaces — the AWS review bot and the GitHub Actions CI reconciler — ran green on the S4 code.
